admission.justification: The choice fixes when and how every leaf closing archives its agents and forbids a wait or a person-driven recovery.

alternatives.option: Archive every recorded leaf agent at once through the host's existing cancel-capable archive call, before the worktrees are removed, whether idle or in a turn.
alternatives.reason: The only moments a leaf is deliberately ended are when its job is done or when it is abandoned; in both the agents have nothing left to do, and the host archive call already ends a running turn. Archiving first keeps no agent working in a folder that is gone.

alternatives.option: Archive only agents observed idle and wait for a running turn to end.
alternatives.reason: The developer rejected the wait: a closed leaf's agents must not linger and potentially cause problems, and an abandoned leaf must not leave an agent running until its turn ends.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The host offers an atomic idle-only archive that cannot end a turn, or the product stops ending leaves while agents run.

alternatives.option: Archive after the worktrees are removed, or leave archival to a person refreshing the host.
alternatives.reason: Removal first lets an agent work for a moment in a folder that no longer exists, and a person-driven archive does not meet the automatic busy/host-down recovery the requirement asks for.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A future requirement moves archival to the host or stops removing worktrees at closing.

alternatives.option: Keep a cap on how many role agents may run at once.
alternatives.reason: The developer withdrew the architect's cap and kept the setting accepted but enforced by nothing for now.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The developer asks for leaf-limit enforcement again.

consequences: The archive attempt is bounded (8 s total, 2 s per call) and never refuses an admitted retirement.
A host failure leaves receipt-owned debt the existing observation loop settles without a person.
context: Finalizing or abandoning a leaf removed its worktrees and branches but left its Worker, Reviewer and Curator in the host as idle sessions. The architect proposed archiving only idle agents; the developer's D56 direction and follow-up words settled what happens to an agent that is in a turn.
decider: Developer direction D56 (2026-10-05) and the developer's follow-up words; implemented under MIK-R76@v1.
